items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: On the boat we met an English singer who was going to India to sing in the Taj Mahal Hotel which was where we would be working also. Her name was Aimee Denton.

ctx.x: Leon Abbey had gone to Chicago and came back with a tenor player named Antony Cosey. The 21st of October we left Paris for Venice, Italy where we took a boat for India. The other musicians were Arthur Lanier, alto and singer, Ollie Tines, drummer, Emil Christian, a white trombone player who had played with the Original Dixieland Band and had lived in England and France a few years. The pianist was Charlie Lewis who had come to Europe with Leon.

We passed through Switzerland which was a beautiful country and arrived in Venice the 22nd of October and that was where the trip started to get interesting. I had read some of the history of Venice and its canals and it says that there is no other city like Venice. We went from the railroad station to the pier by taxi gondolas and watched the way the gondolier guided the gondola and the traffic on the canals. It was a real sight to see. From the pier there was a launch that took us to the ship we were to sail…

The weather was beautiful in Venice and we left the port in the afternoon. The following day we rented deck chairs and I began to get better acquainted with the musicians whom I had not known much about before. This was Leon's second time to be engaged at the Taj. Charlie Lewis was known as "Dizzy" and "Dizzy" called Leon "Dog". We started calling Cosey "Bags" because he had a ruptured testicle which really showed, but it didn't seem to bother him physically. He in turn called everybody "funny looking", even…
